submission.justification: Crystal-K1 at 5 cm gives the best 662 keV FWHM of the three candidates: 3.03% in the original run and 2.83% on rerun. K1 was the best candidate at 2, 5 and 10 cm, and 5 cm was the best thickness for all three crystals. The 10 cm result was reproduced on rerun (4.03% vs 2.83% at 5 cm), so the degradation is treated as real, though its physical cause is undocumented. Low-background suitability is NOT verified. No project document gives K-40, La-138, Lu-176 or Th/U data, a background budget, or radiopurity limits for any candidate, so this recommendation rests on resolution alone. Vendor radiopurity certification for K1 is required before procurement. If K1 fails that check, the fallback is K2 at 5 cm (4.45% FWHM). K3 is not recommended (9.10%). Efficiency was not simulated. Shielding (20 cm Pb, 5 cm OFHC Cu) and the boil-off nitrogen radon purge are already in place. Note that K1's high light yield and fast decay do not by themselves establish radiopurity, and high-light-yield scintillators can carry intrinsic activity, so the certification check is the decisive step.
